text: Subscribe to skip adsAdvertisementZoologyWatch Norway’s Lice-Zapping Robots Protect Salmon FarmsI bet that feels good for the salmonJCBy Jake Currie9:00 AM CST on November 13, 2026Add Nautilus to GoogleHumans and bears aren’t the only animals that find salmon delicious. Salmon lice, small marine crustaceans, attach themselves to the fish and make a meal of their blood, mucus, and skin cells (not my favorite part of the salmon, but it takes all types). These parasites are also the scourge of Norwegian salmon farmers, who keep their shoals in net pens in the Atlantic Ocean. Removing them is required by law, but it’s a real pain. They’ve become resistant to pharmaceutical deterrents and traditional delousing methods involve hot water baths, scrubbing, and general rough handling, which can damage or kill the fish. While some farms have employed cleaner wrasses to feed on the bloodsuckers, they’ve proved difficult to keep alive. Read more: “Cocaine Fish: How Salmon Behave When Amped Up on Coke”Subscribe to skip adsAdvertisement
